Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates enlarged central pulmonary arteries with abrupt tapering (pruning) of the peripheral vessels and cardiomegaly with right ventricular enlargement, which are classic radiographic signs of pulmonary hypertension. In a 52-year-old woman presenting with right-sided heart failure, this pattern is highly suggestive of pulmonary hypertension secondary to a long-standing left-to-right shunt like an atrial septal defect (Eisenmenger syndrome), where the "peripheral nodules" described in other options are actually dilated peripheral pulmonary arteries.
